attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The claim is a description of how LLMs work. The normalised wording matches the statement.

contract.note: Reading 'autocomplete' as describing the mechanism, and 'database' in the post's own sense, is fair and ordinary. It is not stretched either way.

evidence.note: A December 2022 preprint states that LMs are trained purely on next-token prediction. This is contemporaneous technical documentation of a text-prediction mechanism.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous technical work describes next-token prediction as the training objective of the LMs of that time, which meets the support condition. Nothing in the packet shows the models mainly retrieve stored records.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A faithful summary of the 'proof of concept, nothing like systems we can count on' assessment of the hybrids that existed then.

contract.note: Measuring dependability by broad testing of December 2022 hybrids is a fair plain reading. Marcus gave no threshold.

evidence.note: A Dec 24, 2022 report says YouChat often gave wrong answers to basic questions. This is anecdotal and covers one product only. It is not broad testing and says nothing about Perplexity.

reviews.rationale: The only outcome evidence is one news report of user-spotted YouChat errors, with no test set or error rate. The contract asks for broad testing, and the packet admits none was found, so the evidence leans toward Marcus but does not meet the support condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The wording keeps 'typically' and 'sometimes weeks or months'.

contract.note: Reading 'update' as refreshing factual knowledge follows the post's own comparison with databases. That is fair.

evidence.note: Targeted factual editing (ROME) was shown in research. That does not establish usual practice in December 2022.
BLOOM's 3.5-month run was initial pretraining, not a factual update.
Continual post-training research for domain adaptation. It is not a record of routine factual refreshes.

reviews.rationale: No item in the packet records how factual updates were usually done in December 2022, or how long they took. The research on editing and continual training is context, not proof of typical practice either way.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The claim is that ChatGPT's knowledge was out of date in December 2022, shown by its not knowing who owned Twitter. The wording is faithful.

contract.note: Requiring independent December 2022 transcripts on ownership is a fair plain reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure says the base model finished training in early 2022. It does not show what ChatGPT actually answered about Twitter's owner.
This is a January 2023 test of a question about the CEO, so it covers a different period and a different fact. It cannot contradict the December ownership claim.

reviews.rationale: There is no independent December 2022 transcript of ChatGPT on Twitter's ownership. The training-date disclosure is only indirect, and the Semafor test comes from a later period and concerns the CEO, so the evidence does not settle the claim.
